chunks.title: Project overview
chunks.text: AnonShield is a local, API-first anonymizer for English documents. It detects personally identifiable information, redacts it, and can restore the exact originals. It has three detector families (regex, checksum, transformer NER), two redaction strategies (placeholder and fake), and is exposed through a REST API, the anon CLI, a Docker image and an MCP server.

chunks.title: Supported scope
chunks.text: AnonShield targets English-language text. The NER model is dslim/bert-base-NER. Regex rules follow US conventions for phone, ZIP and dates. Checksum validation is international (IBAN mod-97, Luhn for cards and French SIREN/SIRET/NIR).

chunks.title: Installation
chunks.text: Create a virtual environment and install the package in editable mode with CPU-only PyTorch: python -m venv .venv then .venv\Scripts\pip install -e ".[dev]" --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu --extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple. Requires Python 3.11 or newer.

chunks.title: Running the API locally
chunks.text: Start the FastAPI app with Uvicorn: .venv\Scripts\uvicorn anonymizer.api:app --reload. It listens on port 8000. Interactive docs are at /docs and the OpenAPI schema is at /openapi.json.

chunks.title: Regex detectors
chunks.text: Regex detectors are deterministic and fast. They emit EMAIL (user@domain.tld), PHONE (US formats such as (555) 123-4567 or +1 555 123 4567), ZIP (12345 or 12345-6789) and DATE (03/15/2024, March 15, 2024, 15 March 2024).

chunks.title: Checksum detectors
chunks.text: Checksum detectors structurally validate identifiers: IBAN with ISO 7064 mod-97, CARD numbers with Luhn (13 to 19 digits), and the French identifiers SIREN and SIRET (Luhn) and NIR (social security number, including Corsica and overseas handling). Invalid checksums are rejected, which removes false positives.

chunks.title: NER detector
chunks.text: NerDetector wraps dslim/bert-base-NER and maps PER to PERSON, ORG to ORGANIZATION, LOC to LOCATION and MISC to MISC. The backbone is capitalization-sensitive, so lowercase names like 'marcus aurelius' can be missed while 'Marcus Aurelius' is found. The model downloads on first use. In the REST API it is opt-in via ner: true.

chunks.title: Overlap resolution
chunks.text: When two entities overlap, the DetectionEngine keeps the higher-ranked span: source priority first (checksum beats regex beats ner), then longer spans, then higher confidence.

chunks.title: Entity shape
chunks.text: Every detector returns the same Entity shape: label, start, end, text, score and source. Because offsets are preserved, redaction is lossless and reversible.

chunks.title: Placeholder redaction
chunks.text: The default strategy replaces each entity with a stable placeholder numbered per label, such as [EMAIL_1], [EMAIL_2] and [PERSON_1]. Bracketed placeholders are unambiguous and safe to match during restore.

chunks.title: Fake value redaction
chunks.text: Pass strategy=fake to replace entities with realistic surrogates generated by Faker, such as a new name, email, IBAN or card number. The mapping still reverses the change. A caveat: a generated surrogate could coincidentally appear elsewhere in the document, so placeholders are safer when round-trip fidelity is critical.

chunks.title: Repeated values
chunks.text: The same (label, value) pair always receives the same replacement. 'John met John' becomes '[PERSON_1] met [PERSON_1]', which keeps the mapping small and consistent.

chunks.title: Restore and mapping lifetime
chunks.text: The API stores mappings in memory with a 15-minute (900-second) TTL via MappingStore. /anonymize returns a mapping_id; pass it to /restore to recover the original text. Unknown or expired ids return HTTP 404. Restarting the API drops all mappings.

chunks.title: API endpoints
chunks.text: The REST API has four endpoints: GET /health for liveness, POST /detect to return entities without changing text, POST /anonymize to redact text and return a mapping id, and POST /restore to recover the original from a mapping id. All request and response bodies are JSON.

chunks.title: POST /detect request
chunks.text: POST /detect takes a JSON body with text (required) and ner (optional boolean, default false). It returns an entities array of {label, start, end, text, score, source}. Setting ner true includes the transformer detector.

chunks.title: POST /anonymize request
chunks.text: POST /anonymize takes text (required), strategy (placeholder or fake, default placeholder) and ner (default false). It returns redacted text, a mapping_id, and the detected entities. Example body: {"text": "Email a@b.com from John Doe", "strategy": "placeholder", "ner": true}.

chunks.title: POST /restore request
chunks.text: POST /restore takes mapping_id and the redacted text. It returns the original text. Example body: {"mapping_id": "map_3f9a1c02", "redacted": "Email [EMAIL_1] from [PERSON_1]"}.

chunks.title: CORS configuration
chunks.text: Allowed browser origins are read from the ANONYMIZER_CORS_ORIGINS environment variable, a comma-separated list. It defaults to http://localhost:3000 for local development. Set it to your deployed frontend origin in production.

chunks.title: CLI usage
chunks.text: The anon command wraps the same engine. anon detect FILE lists entities. anon anonymize FILE -o OUT [--strategy fake] writes redacted text plus an OUT.mapping.json sidecar. anon restore FILE --mapping OUT.mapping.json -o OUT reverses it. anon version prints the version. PDFs are supported when they have a text layer.

chunks.title: Docker usage
chunks.text: Build the CPU-only image with docker build -t anonymizer-api . and run it with docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 anonymizer-api, or docker compose up --build. The image installs PyTorch from the CPU index so it stays small and needs no GPU. The API listens on 0.0.0.0:8000.

chunks.title: MCP server
chunks.text: The MCP server exposes three tools: detect(text), anonymize(text, strategy) and restore(mapping_id, redacted). Start it with python -m anonymizer.mcp_server over stdio. Register it in Claude Desktop or Cursor via an mcpServers entry whose command is python and args are -m anonymizer.mcp_server.

chunks.title: Evaluation harness
chunks.text: The eval harness generates English documents with known PII spans and reports micro-averaged precision, recall and F1. Run python -m eval.run -n 200 --seed 0. Add --ner to include the transformer model. The regex plus checksum pipeline scores 1.000 on the synthetic set by construction.

chunks.title: Limitations
chunks.text: Known limitations: NER is capitalization-sensitive and misses lowercase names; long documents are not windowed yet; regex formats target US conventions; the REST API accepts text only (PDF extraction is CLI-only); fake surrogates can collide on restore; mappings are in-memory with a 900-second TTL; and there is no authentication or rate limiting in this build.

chunks.title: Deployment
chunks.text: The docs and tester are a Next.js app deployed on Vercel. The FastAPI backend cannot run on Vercel serverless because CPU PyTorch exceeds the function size limit, so it runs as the Docker image on a container host such as Render, Railway, Fly.io or Hugging Face Spaces. The frontend calls it via NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL, and the backend allows the frontend origin through ANONYMIZER_CORS_ORIGINS.
